html:
SMTO-EXE-0134 — A web browser step was too big for SMTO to handle

GUID: 3bd14311-d4e9-55e7-9ca9-76c1ccfa7730
Slug: browser-size-limit
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • The browser step went over one of SMTO's limits, such as a file larger than 16 MB, a description that matched too many things on the page, or too many open tabs. SMTO stopped that step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were uploading or downloading a file, use a file smaller than 16 MB, for example by compressing it or splitting it into parts. Files moved through the web browser are limited to 16 MB, and larger ones are refused.
  2. If SMTO was looking for something on the page, tell it exactly which button, link or field you mean, using the words shown on it. A vague description can match more than 1,000 things on a page, which SMTO refuses to handle.
  3. Ask SMTO to close browser tabs it no longer needs before opening another one. Each browser session can have at most 32 tabs open.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the step and reports the file, item or tab it used.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying what you were trying to do. If you need a file larger than 16 MB, ask them for another way to move it; don't share your website sign-in details to work around the limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Browser request, output, file or tab capacity exceeded a supported limit (over 1,000 locator matches, a file or screenshot over 16 MiB, a viewport over 16 million pixels, or 32 tabs in a session).

What this means

  • Browser bounds rejected excessive element matches, file-transfer bytes, tab count or other bounded output. The category is not limited to a large file. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Browser bounds rejected excessive element matches, file-transfer bytes, tab count or other bounded output. The category is not limited to a large file.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the exact bound: broad locator, snapshot/output size, upload/download size or session tab count.

How to fix it

  • Identify the limit from the operation: narrow the locator (specific role and name, label or test_id) when it matches more than 1,000 elements; keep uploads, downloads and screenshots under FILE_LIMIT (16 MiB) in src/gateway_core/browser/contract.py; or close unneeded owned tabs (32 per session). Oversized downloads are deleted from the browser's temporary storage and marked rejected_size.
  • Narrow the locator or output, use a supported bounded file, or close unneeded owned tabs according to the specific bound.

Retry and execution caution

  • Narrow the page selection or use a smaller file. Browser transfers are limited to 16 MiB and snapshots to 200 elements.

How to verify the fix

  • A narrower valid request or deliberately reduced session load stays within bounds while preserving required evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
